subject: Art & Design
title: Web Fonts: Typography Goes Online
description: A quick win: understand Web Fonts: Typography Goes Online.

hook.text: In 2005, the web had about 10 fonts. Today, Google Fonts alone offers over 1,500 — all free.

buildup.text: @font-face in CSS let websites load custom fonts. Before that, you were stuck with system defaults.

discovery.text: Web fonts download to the user's browser. File size matters — a heavy font slows the whole page.

twist.text: FOUT (Flash of Unstyled Text) happens when the page loads before the font. Users see a jarring swap.

climax.text: font-display: swap tells the browser to show fallback text immediately, then swap when the font loads.

punchline.text: Beautiful type means nothing if the page is too slow to read.

quiz.question: What is FOUT in web typography?
options: Flash of Unstyled Text — fallback font showing before custom font loads
A type of font file format

details.summary: Web fonts — loaded from servers via CSS @font-face — freed web typography from the limitation of system-installed fonts. Before web fonts, websites were restricted to Arial, Times, Georgia, and a handful of others.
details.whyItMatters: Web fonts were a revolution for digital design. They gave web designers the same typographic freedom print designers had always enjoyed, enabling brand-consistent typography across all platforms and devices.
takeaways: Web fonts load from servers via CSS @font-face declarations
They freed web design from system font limitations
Thousands of fonts are now available for any website

faq.question: Do web fonts affect page load speed?
faq.answer: Yes. Each font file adds 20-100KB to page load. Multiple weights and styles compound the cost. Performance strategies include using font-display: swap to prevent invisible text, subsetting to include only needed characters, preloading critical fonts, and limiting the number of web fonts used.

faq.question: What is the FOIT/FOUT problem?
faq.answer: FOIT (Flash of Invisible Text) hides text until the web font loads, causing a blank content flash. FOUT (Flash of Unstyled Text) shows the fallback font first, then swaps. FOUT is generally preferred because content is accessible immediately, though the visual shift can be jarring.
